Stage <code> of the <programme> programme, wave <n>. Status and order: the programme's table in `ROADMAP.md`.

## In short

For anyone, without the code: what goes wrong today, for whom, with one example, and what the library will do
differently once this is done. No module names, refusal codes or file paths in this section.

## Technical detail

What changes and where, for an engineer: modules, functions, files, refusal and rule codes, the order of the
work. A code follows its meaning: "a reaction to another context's event that leaves delivery out (X10)".
Name files, never line numbers: they go stale before the issue closes.

## In scope

-

## Out of scope

- … because …

## Outcome

What is true once it is done, for a host, a user of the library or this repository: a state of things, not a list
of tasks.

## Judge

The check that shows the outcome, which anyone can start: a test, `mix check`, a task and its output, a page. If
none exists yet, the first part of the work builds it. If none can exist, say so, and name what a maintainer
checks instead.

## Expected result

What the judge shows once it is done: a refusal, a warning, a page, a test that passes.

## Decisions

Recorded as comments when they are made: what was chosen, the options that lost and why, and who decided.

## Changes to the design record

The dated amendments this stage made in `docs/adr/`, each linking back here, or "none".

## For applications using the library

What a host has to do when it upgrades, or "nothing".
